name: get_context
summary: Read task or artifact context by key or id
description: Read one task or artifact by key or id. Task context comes from the task context endpoint (it includes parentId, estimate and threadUrl, the link to the thread working on the task). Pass comments:true to include the task thread, subtasks:true to include its subtasks as a nested tree of any depth (subtasks), depth to stop at that many levels. The wire type stays issue. Example: {"id":"CORA-142","subtasks":true}.

type.description: Only when the kind cannot be inferred from the id. issue is the task discriminator.

comments.description: Tasks only: include the comment thread (last 20).

subtasks.description: Tasks only: include the subtasks as a nested tree (each node's subtasks hold its children, to any depth).

depth.description: With subtasks: levels to include, 1 = direct children only. Default: all.

name: find_work
summary: Find tasks with filters (assignee `me`, status, project…)
description: Find tasks to work on. Filters: q, assignee ('me' or user id), status, priority, kind, projectId, parentId (only the direct subtasks of that task, by key or id), open (default true), and limit. There is no team filter. Use get_context for detail, with subtasks:true for a task's whole subtask tree.

parentId.description: Key or id of a task: only its direct subtasks.

name: search
summary: Full-text search across every object type; run it before creating anything
description: Full-text search across supported object types: tasks, projects and artifacts. The type token for a task is still issue. Run it before creating anything so you reuse what exists. `types` narrows the results. Returns type, id, key, title and subtitle.

name: get_insights
summary: Where the problems are: stale or overdue tasks, bottlenecks, stuck PRs, flow metrics, agent failures
description: Where are the problems? Health signals for blocked or stale tasks, bottlenecks, PRs stuck in review, failing CI, flow metrics and agent failures. Use it to decide what needs attention before picking work. Narrow with projectId; days is 7, 30 or 90. The full list behind one signal: run_tool {name:'get_insight_signal', arguments:{id:'<signal>'}}.

name: get_workspace
summary: Workspace settings: label ids, estimate scale
description: The workspace and its settings: label catalog (ids to pass as `labels`), estimateScale (none, fibonacci, linear, exponential, tshirt). Read it once before filing tasks so you assign real label ids and a valid estimate. Takes no arguments.

name: list_projects
summary: Projects; filter by repository string to find the project of a checkout
description: Projects group related tasks. Filter by repository (owner/name or URL, case-insensitive; matched here, not by the API) to find the project of this checkout, or by q, status, leadId. One match is 'this project'; several: ask which. Then find_work {projectId} lists its tasks. Returns id, key (the task key prefix), name, status, priority, lead, repository and dates; read one project fully with run_tool get_project.

repository.description: owner/name or a git URL of the checkout.

q.description: Text filter on the project name.

name: create_task
description: File one task after checking for duplicates. Tasks are the unit of work. Use parentId to create a sub-task; sub-tasks keep independent statuses and can be nested. There is no team. source defaults to agent. Labels are ids from get_workspace settings.labels, never names.

title.description: The symptom or request in plain words, under ~80 chars.

body.description: Markdown: steps, expected vs actual, where you saw it.

parentId.description: Id or key of the parent task.

estimate.description: Only when the size is clear and the workspace uses estimates.

threadUrl.description: Link to the Delta thread working on this task (http or https).

force.description: Create even if an open task has the same title.

name: update_task
summary: Change a task's status, priority, assignee, labels, parent, duplicate marker…
description: Update one task: status, priority, assignee, labels, estimate (points; null clears), title/body, project, milestoneIds, threadUrl (link to the thread working on it; null clears), parentId (moves it under another task as a subtask, or null for a root task), kind (classification only; it does not change the key), duplicateOfId (marks a duplicate of another task). Changing project re-keys the task and keeps its old key as an alias. Sub-tasks keep independent statuses and can be nested. There is no team. null clears an optional field. Set in_progress when you start (the server assigns you if you are a user and nobody is), in_review while the PR is open, done ONLY once the fix is merged. Never close what you did not verify. Several tasks at once: triage_tasks. Example: {"idOrKey":"CORA-142","status":"in_review"}.

name: start_work
summary: Pick up a task: context, safety checks, marks the start
description: Start work on a task: load task context and set it in_progress. Completed and canceled tasks are not changed. Pass a short plan to leave it as a comment.

plan.description: One comment: what you will do.

name: report_progress
summary: Record artifacts, task status and a comment
description: Record task progress: artifact, issueStatus, and/or comment. issueStatus is the wire name for the task status. Do not set a task done until its fix is verified and merged.

issue.description: Task key or id (for issueStatus, artifacts and comments). The argument name stays issue.

externalId.description: PR number, sha, build id: used to find the existing artifact.

description.description: Only used when the artifact is created.

issueStatus.description: New status of the task. in_review while its PR is open; done only once merged.

comment.description: One factual comment on the task.

name: track_time
summary: Your timer: start or stop it on a task, see what runs, list, add or delete entries
description: The signed-in person's task timer (needs a key that acts as a user, not a custom token). action: start (task = key or id; stops a timer already running), stop, status (the running timer and its task), list (your 100 latest entries, optionally of one task, with durations and a total), add (a finished entry: task, startedAt and endedAt as ISO-8601 with a zone, e.g. 2026-05-01T09:00:00Z), delete (entryId). Entries are always your own. Example: {"action":"start","task":"CORA-142"}.

task.description: Task key or id (start, add; filters list).

projectId.description: Project to book the time on when there is no task.

description.description: What you work on (start, add), at most 500 characters.

startedAt.description: add: ISO-8601 start with a zone.

endedAt.description: add: ISO-8601 end with a zone, after startedAt.

entryId.description: delete: the time entry id (te_…) from list.

name: attach_artifact
summary: Attach or update a PR, build or link on a task
description: Attach proof of work or a reference to a task: pull request, build, test report, deployment, design or link. Idempotent when the same external id or URL is repeated. Pass issue for the task.

externalId.description: PR number, sha, build id: used to find the existing artifact.

description.description: What it is / why attached (only used on create).

name: add_comment
summary: Comment on any object by key or id
description: Comment on a task, project, or artifact by key or id. The wire subject type for a task is issue. Use for a factual note after a meaningful step; skip trivial steps because the activity log records changes.

on.description: Key or id of what you comment on.

type.description: Only when the kind cannot be inferred. issue is a task.

name: triage_tasks
summary: Triage up to 25 tasks in one call (priority, duplicates, grouping)
description: Triage up to 25 tasks in one call: priority, duplicate marker, assignment, project, status, labels, and comment. Items fail independently. There is no team.

issue.description: Task key or id. The argument name stays issue.

duplicateOf.description: Key or id of the original task.

name: list_capabilities
summary: Discover the full catalog: search it, get a tool's schema and how to call it
description: Discover the long tail beyond this tool list: every Trama operation your key may use. No arguments: groups with counts. q or group: matching tools with a one-line summary. tool:'<name>': full detail with the exact input schema and how to call it. Then run it with run_tool. Use it when none of the task tools above fits, instead of guessing names. Example: {"q":"milestone"} then {"tool":"create_milestone"}.

q.description: Words that must all appear in a tool's name, description or route.

group.description: Resource group, e.g. tasks, projects, milestones.

tool.description: Exact tool name: returns its schema and call example.

all.description: Also list tools your key cannot use (marked unavailable).

name: run_tool
summary: Run any catalog operation by name, with the usual validation and permissions
description: Run any operation found with list_capabilities by its name, with that tool's own arguments. Arguments are validated against the tool's schema and the API checks your key's permissions on every call, exactly as if the tool were listed. Example: {"name":"create_milestone","arguments":{"projectId":"pj_…","name":"Beta"}}. For a route no tool covers use api_request.
